source_scope: Dyachenko arXiv:2511.07465v1 only, plus local prior audit as read-only context

hypotheses.claim: The alpha in Lemma 7.2 is the squarefree kernel factor of delta.
hypotheses.evidence: PDF v1 p.16, Lemma 7.2: delta=alpha*d'^2 with alpha square-free.

hypotheses.claim: The alpha in Theorem 9.21(III) is defined as gcd(g,b'+c').
hypotheses.evidence: PDF v1 p.28, lines for Theorem 9.21(III): alpha:=gcd(g,b'+c'), d'=g/alpha.

hypotheses.claim: Theorem 9.21(I)'s assertion that the two alpha/d' descriptions are consistent holds for every admissible ED2 row.
hypotheses.evidence: P=37, (delta,b,c)=(5,5,10), g=5,b'=1,c'=2: alpha_lattice=1,d_lattice=5, but delta=5 != 25.

hypotheses.claim: The P=37 failure is caused by a nonprimitive normalized pair.
hypotheses.evidence: gcd(1,2)=1; the row is primitive under the displayed normalization.

hypotheses.claim: The section 7 use of g can be read simultaneously as gcd(b,c) and alpha*d'.
hypotheses.evidence: Lemma 7.2 first sets g=gcd(b,c), then says set g:=alpha*d'; P=29 example has constructed g=2 but gcd(4,8)=4.

hypotheses.claim: For every integer t>=1, P=8t-3 and (delta,b,c,A)=(t,t,2t,2t) satisfy the ED2 identity.
hypotheses.evidence: 4bc-b-c=t(8t-3)=P*delta and A=bc/delta=2t.
hypotheses.inspection: symbolic identity and Fraction for t<=10000

hypotheses.claim: When P=8t-3 is prime, the family is an admissible positive three-term decomposition.
hypotheses.evidence: 4/P=1/(2t)+1/(tP)+1/(2tP), with 2t<tP<2tP for t>=1 and P>2.

hypotheses.claim: For prime P=8t-3>3, the lattice alpha is gcd(t,3)=1; when t is odd, the displayed Theorem 9.21(I) gcd conditions also hold.
hypotheses.evidence: If 3 divides t then 3 divides P; impossible for a prime P>3. The remaining conditions are gcd(1,t)=1 and gcd(2,t)=1, the latter requiring odd t.

hypotheses.claim: For every prime family row with t>1 the numerical compatibility fails; for the odd-t subfamily satisfying Theorem 9.21(I)'s displayed gcd conditions, it is a direct theorem-I counterexample.
hypotheses.evidence: alpha_lattice=1,d_lattice=t, so the asserted value is t^2 while delta=t.
hypotheses.inspection: all prime rows P<=1,000,000; theorem-I admissible subrows separated by gcd(2,t)=1

hypotheses.claim: The boundary t=1 (P=5) is the only family point where the two numerical delta expressions agree.
hypotheses.evidence: t=t^2 iff t=1 for positive integers.

hypotheses.claim: Squarefree t subfamily gives literal primitive Section 7 parameter rows, so the P=37 example is not rescued by a non-squarefree caveat.
hypotheses.evidence: P=13 (t=2), P=37 (t=5), P=101 (t=13), and further rows have alpha_sf=t,d_sf=1,g=t,b'=1,c'=2.

hypotheses.claim: The family mismatch is not a P=37 numerical accident.
hypotheses.evidence: Independent prime scan records a mismatch for every P=5 mod 8, P>5, in the stated range.

hypotheses.claim: The mismatch also appears in squarefree-alpha template rows generated from the paper's product identity.
hypotheses.evidence: Enumerate (alpha,d,b',c') from c'=(Pd+b')/(4alpha*d*b'-1), with primitive filters.

hypotheses.claim: Direct ED2 enumeration is needed to distinguish a template defect from a defect in the underlying unit-fraction identity.
hypotheses.evidence: Direct b,c enumeration checks 4bc-b-c=Pdelta, delta|bc, ordering, and Fraction independently.

hypotheses.claim: The unit-fraction decomposition itself fails on the mismatch rows.
hypotheses.evidence: Fraction equality is true for P=13,37,101 and all scanned family rows; the issue is parameter compatibility, not the decomposition.

hypotheses.claim: The paper's P=29 worked example satisfies the displayed primitive gcd condition.
hypotheses.evidence: Displayed alpha=1,d'=2,b'=2,c'=4 gives gcd(b',c')=2, while the displayed g=2 and b=4,c=8 have gcd(b,c)=4.

hypotheses.claim: P=37 is a valid concrete ED2 row satisfying primitive normalization and exposing the alpha collision.
hypotheses.evidence: (delta,b,c,A)=(5,5,10,10), (b',c')=(1,2), all integer and Fraction checks pass; lattice prediction is 25.

hypotheses.claim: A safe notation repair is to use alpha_sf,d_sf for delta=alpha_sf*d_sf^2 and alpha_lat,d_lat for gcd(g,b'+c') and g/alpha_lat.
hypotheses.evidence: The two definitions are individually well-defined but are not equal on P=37.

hypotheses.claim: The equality delta=alpha_lat*d_lat^2 must be an additional compatibility hypothesis, not a consequence of the lattice definition.
hypotheses.evidence: It is exactly the condition that fails on the family and can be checked without factorization.

hypotheses.claim: The alpha mismatch alone refutes the stated proof route but not necessarily Theorem 9.21's existential conclusion.
hypotheses.evidence: The source's geometric argument may use a restricted constructed subfamily; the v1 text does not prove the needed compatibility.

hypotheses.claim: The correction candidate has no direct implication for the truth of the Erdos-Straus conjecture.
hypotheses.evidence: All tested rows remain valid decompositions; only a claimed parameter identification is contradicted.

hypotheses.claim: The result is suitable for pre-audit as a possible corrigendum note, not as a new ESC solution or a novelty claim.
hypotheses.evidence: Primary-source wording, explicit P=37 counterexample, symbolic family, and independent verifier are all available.

hypotheses.claim: The issue may be a repairable variable reset/overloading rather than a fatal theorem counterexample.
hypotheses.evidence: A corrected theorem would need an explicit distinction between constructed scale g and gcd(b,c), plus a proof of the compatibility condition.
